key_gap: AI computed the same posterior (0.87, resolved YES) but took the outside view as a post-hoc sanity check instead of leading with the reference class, framed the deliverable as a band around a point prediction rather than a scoreable probability with calibration framing, and buried the revision rule in the packet instead of committing it as a tracked trigger.
learning_signal: For forecast tasks with a resolvable outcome and given evidence, ordering and form are trainable: reference-class/base-rate estimation must precede inside-view evidence processing; the deliverable is a probability with a range and a falsifiable revision rule; Brier scoreability is a hard requirement that point predictions fail.
suggested_improvement: In WHAT for forecast-class tasks, require (a) an explicit outside-view pass before inside-view evidence (gate on ordering), (b) probability-form output with range, and (c) a named revision rule with trigger values; in REVIEW, score the forecast's Brier against resolution when available and feed it back.

key_gap: The pure style applied probability machinery to a category-new one-off with 2 data points and produced precision theater: a 90% CI [8.2k–11.5k] from a 0-residual-df fit that missed the actual outcome (2,900) by >3 sd of its own model, and three probability moves driven by non-metric news events (updating without new information).
learning_signal: Superforecasting machinery is a precision tool that must first ask whether precision is warranted: thin evidence (small n, no reference class) requires a deliberately wide range, a probability held flat across non-information events, and the decision lever separated from the forecast; the AI's evidence-gap gate (NEEDS_EVIDENCE) stopped exactly what the pure style did not.
suggested_improvement: Add a precision-warrant check in WHAT/WHY for forecast tasks: compute residual degrees of freedom (n and fit parameters); if df is ~0 or no reference class exists, force (a) a wide range, (b) an explicit no-update-without-new-information statement in HOW, and (c) a decision-action section independent of the calibrated probability.
